Closing — this is intended behavior from Anthropic's side, not a bug we can fix.

Anthropic forces the `mcp_` tool-name prefix as the only pathway through which OAuth subscription tokens (Pro/Max) can access tools at all. The subscription-token tool access they allow is metered against the overage/extra-usage bucket exclusively — there is no "included quota" path for tools on OAuth subscriptions. Removing the prefix doesn't unlock the included quota; it would block all tool-bearing requests on subscription tokens entirely.

The trade-off is intentional: keep the prefix and have tools work for users who have overage enabled (or pay-per-use), or drop the prefix and break tools for every OAuth subscription user. We chose the former.

For Max/Pro subscribers without overage enabled: use an API key instead of the OAuth subscription token, or enable usage-based billing on your Anthropic account.

Following up on my earlier comment — I built the localhost adapter I described.

**[claude-hermes-subscription-adapter](https://github.com/eliaspfeffer/claudehermessubscriptionadapter)**

It's a small FastAPI server that sits between Hermes and Anthropic:

```
Hermes → localhost:8082 (adapter) → claude -p (CLI) → Anthropic
```

Because requests go through the Claude Code CLI instead of a raw OAuth token, they hit your normal subscription quota rather than the overage/extra-usage bucket.

### Setup (2 steps)

**1. Start the adapter**
```bash
git clone https://github.com/eliaspfeffer/claudehermessubscriptionadapter
cd claudehermessubscriptionadapter
pip install -r requirements.txt
python server.py          # listens on http://127.0.0.1:8082
```

**2. Point Hermes at it** — edit `~/.hermes/config.yaml`:
```yaml
model:
  default: claude-opus-4-7
  provider: anthropic
  base_url: http://127.0.0.1:8082
providers:
  anthropic:
    api_key: dummy          # value is ignored, the CLI handles auth
    base_url: http://127.0.0.1:8082
```

Then just run `hermes` as normal. Tested and working today with Hermes 0.14.0 and Claude Code 2.1.145.

### How tool calls work

The adapter converts Anthropic tool definitions into instructions appended to the system prompt and teaches Claude to emit calls as `<tool_call>{"name":"…","input":{…}}</tool_call>` blocks, which it then parses back into proper `tool_use` content blocks. Multi-turn tool loops work because Hermes sends `tool_result` messages back, which the adapter serialises into the conversation context passed to `claude -p`.

Prerequisites: Claude Code CLI installed and authenticated (`claude -p "hi"` works in your terminal).

In your hermes installation (in my case, on Windows, C:\Users\[yourUser]\AppData\Local\hermes) is a file ".env". I fetched my API from https://platform.claude.com/dashboard and made a line in that .env file at the very beginning
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=[put your API key here]
